subject: learning/supervisor-coordination-ref-push-hook-isolation
statement: Parentless task claims and refs/pyxis evidence-store commits are supervisor-owned coordination state, not branch code. Their Git operations need the existing scoped policy that disables repository hooks and fsmonitor for the individual command; ordinary branch publication must continue through the repository's required gates.
intent: Allow claims and durable review/evidence compare-and-swap updates to coexist with composed repository hooks without executing repository code outside verification or bypassing feature-branch gates.
rationale: The real installed Forgejo E2E failed after composed hooks were enabled because claim acquisition pushed a parentless coordination commit through a pre-push gate that tried to find a merge base with the feature base branch. Fetching more branch history cannot create ancestry for an intentionally parentless claim. Persistent repository-wide hook changes or relaxing the gate would cross the wrong boundary; only supervisor-owned coordination operations should carry command-scoped core.hooksPath=/dev/null and core.fsmonitor=false, while retaining their existing CAS expected-head checks.
fit_criterion: The installed regression uses real Pyxis/docgate binaries, the installed payload, composed hooks, and a local bare Git remote. Supervisor claim acquisition/release and refs/pyxis evidence update/readback succeed; ordinary pushes of the same orphan claim object to a branch or a manual metadata ref are rejected by the real merge-base gate; a valid branch push succeeds. The parent-checkout guard remains active, core.hooksPath is unchanged, and parent HEAD is preserved.
